title: arXiv mathematics — 30 October 2026 batch: 10 notable papers
global_caveat: This is an inferred ranking, not an official arXiv trending chart; arXiv publishes no such chart, and the selected papers are too new for robust citation-based attention evidence. Read as notable recent papers, not measured popularity.

sections.title: The Number of Tropical Order Types and Coherent Matching Fields
sections.abstract: The authors bound counts of coherent matching fields, tropical hyperplane sequences, regular triangulations, and labeled order types, comparing the combinatorial expressivity of linear programs and mean-payoff games.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-way cross-listing across combinatorics, algebraic geometry, and optimization/control; matching first-order asymptotics for related structures; answers Santos's named counting question about regular triangulations.
sections.claimed_result: For fixed rank, the number of regular triangulations of Δ^{n−1}×Δ^{r−1} is n^{(r−1)^2 n+o(n)}; the paper also compares real and signed-tropical labeled order types and shows a collapse after double tropicalization. The paper states Theorems 1.1–1.4 and Corollary 1.2.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: As n tends to infinity, rank/dimension is fixed; counts concern labeled structures and general-position tropical hyperplane sequences.
sections.unique_caveat: First-order counts do not settle every finer or unlabeled enumeration question and should not be read as uniform in rank.

sections.title: A Sharp Uniqueness-Nonuniqueness Dichotomy for Neutral Vortex Arrays in 2D Euler Equations
sections.abstract: For stationary arrays of disjoint neutral vortices, the authors give an integral test on vorticity L^p growth separating uniqueness for every datum in the class from existence of a datum with two distinct evolutions.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A sharp two-sided criterion within a precisely defined Euler data class, with both uniqueness and a matching nonuniqueness construction; paired thematically with a same-batch fixed-p nonuniqueness result.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.3 states that I_Θ=∫_{p0}^∞dp/Θ(p) diverging gives uniqueness for every datum in the stationary neutral-array class, while a finite integral yields a datum with two distinct unforced Lagrangian Euler evolutions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Two-dimensional incompressible Euler on R^2; compactly supported stationary arrays of disjoint radial neutral vortices, with a finite nondecreasing envelope controlling all finite vorticity L^p norms.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors explicitly leave unresolved whether the classical Yudovich uniqueness threshold is sharp for general unbounded vorticities; this result uses restricted array geometry and exact shielding.

sections.title: JT gravity as a conformal scaling limit of random flat combinatorial disks
sections.abstract: A Boltzmann ensemble of rectilinear combinatorial disks converges, after rescaling a distinguished side to large length, to a continuum random surface described by flat Jackiw–Teitelboim gravity.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Connects discrete random geometry, probability, and mathematical physics; provides a branching-exploration criterion intended to transfer the scaling-limit proof to other discrete disk models.
sections.claimed_result: Theorem 1.1 proves convergence in distribution of uniformly parametrized conformal factors of Boltzmann rectilinear disks, after subtracting log B, to the flat JT surface as base length B tends to infinity. Theorem 1.3 gives a general criterion based on Markov exploration, tightness, and convergence of exploration data.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The proved model is the critical Boltzmann ensemble of rectilinear flat disks with a distinguished base; convergence is uniform on compact subsets in the stated conformal coordinates. The general criterion has additional exploration hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper proves the limit for this ensemble, not all discretizations of flat surfaces; extensions to triangulations or quadrangulations are proposed as a route, not proved here.

sections.title: On Zeros and Algorithms for Disordered Systems II: The Antiferromagnetic Ising Model up to Kesten-Stigum
sections.abstract: The authors give a polynomial-time, arbitrarily accurate partition-function estimator for the antiferromagnetic Ising model on a uniformly random regular graph up to the Kesten–Stigum threshold, using a high-probability zero-free region.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Four-category cross-listing and a concrete algorithmic result tied to a zero-free theorem; the abstract identifies the threshold as the full replica-symmetric regime and a conjectured boundary for efficient counting and sampling.
sections.claimed_result: The authors claim the first polynomial-time algorithm achieving arbitrarily high accuracy for the partition function throughout the stated inverse-temperature range, and prove Fisher zeros are absent from a constant-width strip around that range with high probability over the random graph.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Antiferromagnetic Ising model on a uniformly random d-regular graph; algorithmic guarantee up to the Kesten–Stigum threshold; zero-free statement holds with high probability over the input graph.
sections.unique_caveat: The paper does not establish tractability beyond the threshold or prove the threshold is optimal; optimality is described as conjectured.

sections.title: A self-normalized law of the iterated logarithm for Rademacher random multiplicative functions
sections.abstract: For a squarefree-supported Rademacher random multiplicative function, the authors prove a two-sided law of the iterated logarithm for partial sums normalized by the full predictable quadratic variation.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A precise almost-sure limit theorem connects probability and number theory, with an explicit random normalization and cluster set rather than only an order-of-magnitude bound.
sections.claimed_result: For M(x)=∑_{n≤x}f(n) and full predictable quadratic variation Q(x), the authors prove limsup M(x)/√(2Q(x)log log x)=1 and liminf=−1 almost surely; the normalized cluster set is [−1,1].
sections.assumptions_and_setting: f is a Rademacher random multiplicative function supported on squarefree integers; Q(x) is the predictable quadratic variation of the martingale obtained by revealing prime signs.
sections.unique_caveat: The authors do not determine whether the separate limsup normalized by √x(log log x)^(1/4) is finite positive with a nondegenerate distribution or infinite almost surely.

sections.title: Supersaturation: Cliques and Positive Square Energy
sections.abstract: A sufficiently large sum of squared positive adjacency eigenvalues forces many copies of a larger clique, with an asymptotically best-possible leading coefficient for each fixed clique size.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: The abstract states a sharp asymptotic supersaturation bound and optimality of its leading coefficient; it links spectral information to extremal clique counts through stability, removal, and cut arguments.
sections.claimed_result: For every fixed r≥2, if √s⁺>(1−1/r)n, then k_{r+1}≥(r^{−(r−1)}−o_r(1))n^{r−1}; the authors say the coefficient is asymptotically best possible, with k_3≥n/2−o(n) for triangles.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: G is a simple graph of order n; r is fixed while n tends to infinity; k_r counts unlabeled K_r copies and s⁺ is the sum of squares of positive adjacency eigenvalues.
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem is asymptotic for fixed r, and its triangle conclusion follows only under the stated spectral threshold.

sections.title: Nonuniqueness of the 2D Euler Evolutions with L^1∩L^p Vorticity
sections.abstract: For every prescribed 1<p<∞, the authors construct compactly supported initial vorticity in L^1∩L^p with two distinct unforced two-dimensional Euler evolutions, both strongly continuous and exactly transported by regular Lagrangian flows.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: A concrete nonuniqueness construction for each finite p, with a mechanism carried through exact Euler patch solutions and a limiting cascade across scales; complements the same-batch envelope dichotomy paper.
sections.claimed_result: For each prescribed 1<p<∞, the paper constructs a compactly supported initial datum in L^1(R^2)∩L^p(R^2) with two distinct evolutions on [0,1], strongly continuous in that space and transported by their respective regular Lagrangian flows.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Unforced incompressible 2D Euler on R^2; the constructed initial vorticity and construction parameters may depend on p.
sections.unique_caveat: The construction is tailored to each prescribed finite p and does not settle uniqueness or nonuniqueness for all unbounded-vorticity classes simultaneously.

sections.title: Multicomplexes in Action: Strong Formality of Compact Hyperkähler Manifolds
sections.abstract: The paper proves compact hyperkähler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in pluripotential homotopy theory, using algebraic results for multicomplexes and commutative n-differential graded algebras.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Three-way cross-listing across algebraic topology, algebraic geometry, and differential geometry; a class-wide formality result is established through a structural algebraic framework.
sections.claimed_result: The author proves all compact hyperkähler manifolds are bigraded strongly formal in the sense of Milivojević and Stelzig, and develops a generalized ∂∂̄-lemma and algebraic formality theorem for the relevant multicomplex setting.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Compact hyperkähler manifolds, interpreted through pluripotential homotopy theory and the paper's notion of bigraded strong formality.
sections.unique_caveat: The specialized formality statement should not be conflated with every version of ordinary rational homotopy formality.

sections.title: Sharp L^2 stability for anisotropic radial Caffarelli-Kohn-Nirenberg inequalities
sections.abstract: The authors prove quantitative stability and sharp constants for radial Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg and Heisenberg inequalities using an anisotropic radial derivative and a smooth strictly convex body's Minkowski functional.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Reports sharp constants, equality-case classification, and weighted L^p extensions; the anisotropic nonsymmetric-body setting broadens the radial formulation.
sections.claimed_result: For the L^2 Caffarelli–Kohn–Nirenberg inequality with a≠b+1, the authors obtain sharp stability constant |b+1−a| and classify equality cases; they also give sharp constants 2 and 4 for scale-invariant and scale-noninvariant L^2 Heisenberg inequalities.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Dimension N≥2 and a smooth strictly convex body, not necessarily origin-symmetric; L^p extensions require 2≤p<∞, a≠b+1, and an additional sign condition.
sections.unique_caveat: The L^2 theorem excludes parameter boundary a=b+1; stated L^p results apply only under additional restrictions.

sections.title: Quantitative propagation of chaos on arbitrary finite time intervals for the three-dimensional repulsive Vlasov-Poisson-Fokker-Planck equation
sections.abstract: For singular repulsive Vlasov–Riesz–Fokker–Planck interactions, the authors prove total-variation propagation-of-chaos rates on finite intervals assuming regularity of the limiting solution, including a three-dimensional Vlasov–Poisson–Fokker–Planck case.
sections.evidence_for_ranking: Addresses singular unregularized interactions and gives a quantitative rate on any finite interval satisfying solution hypotheses; the proof combines weighted BBGKY estimates with coupling.
sections.claimed_result: The authors prove algebraic-in-particle-number convergence of marginals in total variation for 0<s<d/2 on R^d or T^d under the stated regularity assumptions; in 3D VPFP they obtain convergence on every finite interval for specified initial-density conditions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Repulsive interactions with singularity |x|^{-s}, 0<s<d/2; product initial law; finite intervals where the limiting classical solution meets required regularity. The 3D VPFP case assumes weighted C^m data, m≥3, Gaussian velocity decay, and spatial decay order M>3.
sections.unique_caveat: The finite-interval result is conditional on regularity of the limiting classical solution, not an unconditional global theorem for arbitrary data.
